# Complete the customer billing-schedule migration

Finish the service-to-customer migration for recurring billing. Creating a customer must create a monthly billing schedule only when that customer has an offering. When an existing customer gains or changes an `offeringId`, replace any previous billing schedule with a customer-level schedule; an already-missing old schedule is not an error. Preserve the authenticated subject and business ID in the scheduler configuration.

Billing jobs receive `businessID` on the scheduler record and `customerId` in `scheduleParameters`. Resolve the customer and its offering, derive the offering billing-cycle time range, call the existing usage-total invoice path with that exact customer and range, and persist a billing record containing the returned invoice ID. Report processing failures through the existing audit channel instead of leaving the queue job with a partially stored billing record.

Route billing scheduler emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` with the `billingReport` consumer name. All non-billing measurements must continue to use the normal scheduler queue and their dimension consumer. Finally, a usage read for a customer without an offering should return an empty result rather than fail.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure and the migration task.

steps.message:
The migration is complete. `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` both pass (44 suites / 82 tests).

## What changed

**Customer → billing schedule ownership** (`src/customer/customer.service.ts`)
- `create` now only schedules recurring billing when the new customer actually has an `offeringId`; otherwise it logs and skips.
- Extracted `createBillingSchedule` (monthly rate, `schedulerID = customerId`, `scheduleParameters: { customerId, businessID }`, carrying `subject` + `businessID`) and `replaceBillingSchedule`, which removes the prior billing-queue schedule — swallowing `NotFoundException` — before creating the customer-level one.
- `update` compares the resulting `offeringId` to the previous one and replaces the schedule when the customer gains or changes an offering (`customer.service.ts:236`).
- `customer.controller.ts:145` now forwards the authenticated `sub` into `update` so the subject is preserved in the scheduler config.

**Billing job is customer/offering driven** (`src/billing/billing.service.ts`)
- Reads `businessID` from the scheduler record (falling back to `scheduleParameters`) and `customerId` from `scheduleParameters`.
- Resolves the customer via `CustomerService.findOne`, returns early when there is no offering, derives the range with `Billing.billingCycleToTimeRange(offering.billingCycle)`, and calls the existing `InvoicesService.generateInvoiceForUsageTotal({ businessID, customerId, start, end })`.
- Persists a `Billing` point containing the returned `invoiceId`, and wraps the whole processor body in a `try/catch` that reports through `AuditService.publishEvent({ topic: AuditScope.ERROR })` instead of throwing out of the queue job.
- `CustomerService` (and the now-unused `ServicesService`) are injected with `@Optional()` so DI stays resolvable; `PrivateAPICustomerModule` was added to `BillingModule`.

**Queue routing** (`src/scheduler/scheduler.service.ts:227`)
- `emitOne` sends `schedulerType.billing` payloads to `scheduler_billing_queue` under `billingScheduleConsumers.billingReport`; everything else still goes to `scheduler_queue` keyed by `dimensionType`.

**Usage read** (`src/usage/usage.service.ts:56`)
- A customer without an offering now returns `[]` (which surfaces as `No Customer usage found`) rather than throwing `ConflictException`.

**Tests added** for each behavior in `customer.service.spec.ts`, `billing.service.spec.ts`, `usage.service.spec.ts`, and a new `scheduler.service.spec.ts`.

One judgement call worth flagging: `Billing.billingCycleToTimeRange` returns `undefined` for any cycle other than `monthly`, so a non-monthly offering will fail and be reported to the audit channel rather than billed. I left that pre-existing gap alone since the task scoped schedules to monthly.
